answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a remotely verified enclave measurement: MRENCLAVE commits to the enclave code, while platform attestation proves it runs on genuine hardware. A copied virtual machine cannot reproduce the hardware-rooted attestation or register the same trusted identity; scaling identities therefore requires additional physical silicon, not cheap VM duplication. This raises the cost of a Sybil spiral, though it does not make hardware acquisition impossible; tide and saffron are merely labels, not security properties.
